newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Norilsk, strike and debt plagued, may issue shares.
newsitem.headline: Norilsk, strike and debt plagued, may issue shares.

text.p: Russia's financially-troubled Norilsk Nickel flagship plant will probably conduct a secondary share issue as part of its debt restructuring plan, a former cabinet official said on Tuesday.
"We will possibly and even likely conduct a secondary share issue," outgoing First Deputy Prime Minister Vladimir Potanin told a news conference.
Potanin is the former chairman of Uneximbank, which owns 51 percent of voting shares in the RAO Norilsk Nickel group, the parent company of the flagship plant.
Workers at the main plant have threatened to disrupt output on March 27 and from April 2 over salary and holiday arrears and related issues.
Potanin said the government had said that a share issue was the only way out of financial crisis, adding that he would return to Uneximbank and work on Norilsk.

He said financial problems at the main plant had been partially resolved through management and other changes but that the company could not count on privileges to finance the vast cost of transporting goods to the Arctic, where it is based.

"Norilsk Nickel, like other enterprises, should pay the state everything it is supposed to, but the government should not demand more than it should" he said, adding that regional budgets should support Norilsk's vast social costs from Norilsk taxes.
